description.html: A compressed coconut coir brick is the most cost-effective way to get a larger amount of substrate. It takes up little space until you use it, and after soaking in water it gives about 70 liters of loose coir. It is a good choice for large terrariums, for several terrariums at once or if you change substrate often.

Coconut coir holds moisture well and releases it slowly, so it suits crested geckos, chameleons, day geckos, tropical snakes and frogs. It is also used as a base in bioactive terrariums. One brick replaces a number of small packs, and as long as it stays dry and sealed, it keeps for a long time.

items: Place the brick in a large container or bucket.
Pour warm water over it and wait until it soaks up the water and starts to break apart.
Break up the lumps by hand until the coir is even.
If it is too wet, squeeze it out before putting it in the terrarium.

description.html: You do not have to prepare the whole brick at once: break off as much as you need and keep the rest dry. The finished coir should be damp but not wet. Browse our other terrarium equipment.
